Prevention: Remove and destroy plant debris from field before planting.
Use tomato plants as repellents; plant them along the field border, at least one month before planting cabbage.
Intercrop mustard with cabbage, this will act as a trap crop for adult moths.
Plant two rows of mustard for every 25 of cabbage.
Use the recommended dose of fertiliser, but split the dose of nitrogen: 4.5kg urea + 13kg
MOP/ropani as a basal dose; 5.5kg urea/ropani as a top dressing 1 month after planting.
After harvest, plough the field to expose any pests harboring in the soil.
A sprinkler irrigation system may reduce the larval population by drowning larvae (first and second instar).
Monitoring: In the standing crop, look for larvae on leaves, holes on leaves, withered leaves, and window pane effect on leaves.
Use control if you see at least one larvae/plant.
Use lure traps to monitor adult moth populations; use water/funnel/Wota
The traps should be suspended about 2-4 feet high, at the field’s edge (trap height should not exceed plant height).
Check traps twice a week early in the morning.
Use control when 5+ adult moths are caught in a trap.
Direct Control: Collect and destroy moth eggs and larvae by crushing or keeping in a bucket of soapy water.
Spray with azadirachtin (neem-based insecticide) (0.03% EC) at 5ml/lit water, using 25lit water /ropani.
DBM pheromone traps to 4 to 6 per ropani.
Bacillus thuringiensis at 1g/lit water, using 25 lit water/ropani.
Benzoate (5% SG) at a rate of 2 gm/16 lit water, using 25 lit water/ropani.
Use a foliar spray of fenvalerate (20% EC) at 0.5 ml/lit water, using 25 lit water /ropani.
Restrictions: Consider a rotation of the pesticides mentioned in this guide if conditions persist and additional treatments are deemed necessary.
Equipment (PPE) such as gloves, masks etc. while mixing and applying insecticides.
Spray a max. of 2 times, with a 15 day interval between sprays.
Spray in the late afternoon, Pre harvest interval (PHI) 3 days.
